text: In Kripke's least fixed-point theory of truth, what is the status of the Liar sentence?
choices: It is valueless — a truth-value gap that receives no value in any fixed point
It is true in the least fixed point
It is false in the least fixed point
It is both true and false
explanation: Kripke uses a partial, three-valued (Strong Kleene) truth predicate; the Liar falls into a truth-value GAP, receiving no value in the least fixed point — indeed in no fixed point, since any value would refute itself. It is not assigned true, false, or (this is a gap, not a glut) both.
